A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification analyses, adversarial-mask experiments, TinyStories feature-circuit results and TinyLlama finetuning experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds FineWeb feature-approximation results, an MNIST HOSVD demonstration and an SAE training-duration study.

M1.justification: The bilinear architecture, feature-basis transformations, eigendecomposition, HOSVD and adversarial-mask construction are retained. The new HOSVD demonstration applies the method already described in v1 Section 3.3; expanded mathematical explanations do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Section 5.2 extends language-feature interpretation from TinyStories to general web text through FineWeb models. FineWeb already appeared in v1's TinyLlama finetuning experiment; the substantive expansion is evaluating eigenvector-based feature interpretation on that broader text population.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain unchanged: ReGLU and SwiGLU in the loss comparison, random adversarial masks, and continued TinyLlama training with fixed activation parameters. Added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Added experiments use 162M- and 335M-parameter FineWeb models, with feature evaluation at approximately two-thirds depth. Appendix H introduces five training-duration conditions for 16x-expansion SAEs at layer 12, evaluated over 100K activations while excluding features with fewer than ten activations. Figure 9 also drops the earlier all-input/pre-TopK correlation series.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests whether HOSVD extracts meaningful shared output directions from the existing MNIST model. New Appendix H examines sensitivity of low-rank feature approximations to SAE training duration, comparing correlation changes with reconstruction metrics. These add substantive analyses beyond the retained regularization, truncation and adversarial studies.

E5.justification: Figure 5 still reports averages over five runs with 90% confidence intervals, and the seed-reporting practice remains unchanged. Appendix H's five SAEs represent different training budgets, not repeated runs or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 9 adds FineWeb correlation curves and distributions and replaces the scatter examples with fw-medium features. New Table 5 reports mean correlations increasing from 0.17 to 0.59 across training-duration conditions, versus normalized MSE changing from 0.17 to 0.15. Appendix D adds HOSVD findings. These are newly reported results under expanded conditions, not demonstrated same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: The symmetry argument, quadratic eigendecomposition, HOSVD formulation and pseudoinverse reconstruction derivation are retained. Added dimension annotations and an explicit SAE activation expression elaborate the existing construction; the new appendices provide empirical analyses rather than new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions and discussion retain the same central claims about interpretable bilinear replacements, low-rank structure and weight-based circuit analysis. The added experiments support those claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix H newly interpret training-dependent correlations as a hidden convergence transition that conventional SAE metrics reveal poorly. Appendix D qualifies HOSVD's interpretability on MNIST and discusses potential utility and computational cost as output classes increase. The existing general limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix G adds FineWeb model specifications, the Mixtral tokenizer and training hyperparameters, including approximately 32B tokens, context length 512 and learning rate 6e-4. Appendix H documents its SAE configuration and evaluation filtering. Table 2 newly discloses TinyStories context length 256; this alone does not establish a changed setting. Code-access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations covering earlier bilinear and polynomial models, tensor decompositions, GLUs and FineWeb. The introduction adds a focused distinction between decomposing input data and extracting features directly from model weights, while retaining the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 expands explanations in Sections 2–4, revises Section 5.2 and adds an author-contributions section. Publication headers and author information change, and inserted appendices trigger renumbering. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 9 is redesigned and relocated to show three models. v2 adds HOSVD Figures 17–18, training-duration Figure 24 and Tables 3 and 5, alongside local panel-label and table-caption adjustments. Most existing visual material retains its design and content.

improvement.justification: v1's direct language-feature evidence centered on a small TinyStories model. v2 substantially strengthens its generality through larger FineWeb models and identifies an important dependence on SAE training duration that reconstruction metrics alone obscure. The HOSVD demonstration also validates a previously unillustrated analysis option. These gains in empirical support and interpretation outweigh the loss of Figure 9's all-input comparison.
